non_blocking_caveats: DISCLOSURE 1 (Prior Inspection of Unseen Datasets): The 4 held-out datasets (FaithDial, WikiBio-GPT3, FEVER, XSum) were examined during zero-shot failure diagnosis before running few-shot adaptation. Therefore, the 40% held-out splits validate few-shot target adaptation on unseen test groups within those datasets, NOT as a completely unexamined external confirmation benchmark.

DISCLOSURE 2 (Statistical Scope of Few-Shot Tests): Paired/one-sample t-tests across 10 seeds quantify variance over adaptation-set draws (holding the 40% test set fixed), while 95% group-bootstrap CIs quantify test-set sampling uncertainty. Both should be reported clearly.
DISCLOSURE 3 (Single-Model Scope): All expanded 10-dataset experiments use frozen TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0. Cross-model generalization to larger 7B-70B LLMs remains future work.

DISCLOSURE 4 (Mitigation Mechanism): On TriviaQA, abstention accounts for the vast majority of system-wide hallucination reduction (112/165 blocked vs. 4/165 actively repaired by Tier 1/2), and 23/85 (27.1%) originally correct answers were abstained. Full regenerative controller comparisons against Entropy/NLL thresholds would require additional GPU generations.

DISCLOSURE 5 (ISP Dominance): In-domain and at K=250 on balanced/moderate targets, ISP alone matches or slightly edges 4-sensor fusion in AUROC; AAS/EEM/DST are justified by zero-shot fallback (EEM on FaithDial/XSum), low-K/severe-imbalance stabilization (XSum K=50/100), low-FPR unique catches, and per-sensor explainability.
